headline: A 2016 law lets a member of Congress give the family of a fallen first responder a flag flown over the Capitol, with a sympathy certificate.
what_it_does: The law lets the Representative or Senator of an immediate family member of a deceased firefighter, police officer, rescue or ambulance crew member, or other public safety officer killed in the line of duty request a Capitol-flown flag for the family. The flag comes with a signed certificate that expresses sympathy. The Speaker of the House or the President pro tempore of the Senate signs it, along with the sponsoring member.
when_it_takes_effect: The summary gives no separate start date, so the law took effect on its enactment date, May 16, 2016.
